title: Methyl Red (MR) Test
principle: Tests for the mixed-acid fermentation pathway of glucose, which produces enough stable acid end-products to maintain a low pH in the medium. Methyl red indicator turns red at low pH and yellow at higher pH.
purpose: Part of the IMViC panel; distinguishes organisms using the mixed-acid fermentation pathway (e.g. E. coli, typically MR-positive) from those using the butanediol fermentation pathway (e.g. Enterobacter species, typically MR-negative), which produces less stable acid and is instead detected by the Voges-Proskauer test.

procedure.instruction: Inoculate MR-VP broth with the test organism and incubate for the full recommended duration — MR requires a longer incubation than many other tests, since the pH must remain stably low, not just transiently drop.
Add several drops of methyl red indicator to the broth.

positiveResult: The broth turns red, indicating a sustained low pH from stable mixed-acid fermentation end-products.
negativeResult: The broth remains yellow/orange, indicating the pH did not remain sufficiently low.
interpretation: MR and VP are often run from the same inoculated broth tube (split for each reagent) and are interpreted together, since most organisms are MR-positive/VP-negative or MR-negative/VP-positive, with both-positive or both-negative results being less common and requiring careful re-checking.
precautions: Incubate for the full recommended duration before testing — reading too early can give a false negative, since pH may not have stabilized yet.
limitations: Reading before the recommended incubation window is complete is the most common source of a misleading result.
